notes: Read the codebook (Datasets.zip, OSF wx7ck) and the manuscript (osf.io/download/ebmf8; Klein et al. 2014, Social Psychology 45(3)). 13 effects over 36 samples (sample; referrer holds the same sites as abbreviations, in ignore). The paper fits no mixed model on the participant rows: per-sample effect sizes are pooled by random-effects meta-analysis (Table 3: "Heterogeneity tests conducted with R-package metafor. REML was used") and moderation by "a Condition x Country (US or other) x Location (lab or online) ANOVA for each effect", so published_model is no; rendered as the condition effect with a random intercept and condition slope per sample, a participant-level proposal, not equivalent to the published meta-analysis. Studies in the paper's order: 1 sunk costs (sunkDV ~ sunkgroup, this row), 2 gain vs loss framing (gainlossDV ~ gainlossgroup, row 2), 3 anchoring (anchoring1-anchoring4 ~ anch1group-anch4group, row 3 the first item), 4 retrospective gambler's fallacy (gambfalDV ~ gambfalgroup), 5 low vs high category scales (scales ~ scalesgroup), 6 norm of reciprocity (reciprocityus ~ reciprocitygroup), 7 allowed/forbidden (allowedforbidden ~ allowedforbiddenGroup), 8 quote attribution (quote ~ quoteGroup), 9 flag priming (flagdv ~ flagGroup, US samples), 10 currency priming (Sysjust ~ MoneyGroup), 11 imagined contact (Imagineddv ~ ContactGroup), 12 sex differences in implicit math attitudes (d_art ~ partgender), 13 implicit vs explicit math attitudes (d_art ~ IATexp.overall); every other dependent variable and its items in ignore. sunkDV is the 1-9 rating of going to the game (sunkcosta paid, sunkcostb free), compared as a mean difference (t-test, ANOVA), so gaussian on the ordinal rating. Hand check #162: stands with corrected notes; 36 samples of 79-1,329 participants.

Many Labs 1 study 2, gain vs loss framing (see row 1): gainlossDV is the program chosen (exact vs probability outcome) after the gain or loss framing (gainlossgroup), tested per sample and pooled by random-effects meta-analysis in the paper; rendered as a logistic model with a random intercept and framing slope per sample. Hand check #162: stands.

Many Labs 1 study 3, anchoring (see row 1): four items, each with its own low or high anchor (anch1group-anch4group); the first item, the distance from San Francisco to New York (anchoring1), is filed, anchoring2-anchoring4 named in row 1.
